# Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation

# Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use mongodump --version in the operating-system terminal to inspect the installed Tools version. MongoDB recommends the latest release and provides the Tools through its Download Center. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/ · keywords: Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md
- [statement] Use the MongoDB Download Center and select the platform and architecture before selecting the package. The installation guide provides Linux deb, rpm and tgz paths, macOS Homebrew and zip paths, and Windows MSI and zip paths. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The current overview documents Database Tools 100.20.1 as supporting MongoDB Server 9.0, 8.3, 8.2, 8.1, 8.0, 7.0, 6.0, 5.0, 4.4 and 4.2. It explicitly says connections to servers earlier than 4.2 fail. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/
- [statement] In DDEV issue 35 on February 11, 2026, a maintainer reported that the Debian Bookworm MongoDB 8.2 ARM64 repository lacked mongodb-database-tools while Ubuntu Noble had it. The reported build error was "E: Unable to locate package mongodb-database-tools". This is a dated repository-availability report, not a claim that all ARM64 platforms are unsupported. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-11) — https://github.com/ddev/ddev-mongo/issues/35
- [statement] For the documented Database Tools 100.20.1 release, MongoDB explicitly excludes Server versions earlier than 4.2 and says connection attempts to earlier versions fail. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Starting with MongoDB 4.4, Database Tools have a release cycle separate from MongoDB Server and use their own versioning, initially 100.0.0. Match a Tools release to its compatibility guidance rather than matching its version number to the server. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump/mongodump-compatibility-and-installation.md · keywords: Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation · also: https://www.prisma.io/dataguide/mongodb/mongodb-database-tools, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/
- [statement] The MongoDB overview documents Database Tools 100.20.1 and lists support for Server 9.0, 8.3, 8.2, 8.1, 8.0, 7.0, 6.0, 5.0, 4.4 and 4.2. This is a version-specific support list, rather than a requirement to install a Server-matching Tools version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The 100.20.0 changelog, released October 26, 2026, states that support for pre-4.2 servers and dump files was removed; both the target server and dump files must be from 4.2 or later. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-tools/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
- [statement] Separate releases do not require a separate installation in every environment: installing MongoDB Server through Homebrew also installs the Database Tools. The standalone Homebrew package is mongodb-database-tools. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md · keywords: Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation · also: https://github.com/mongodb/homebrew-brew
- [statement] For a standalone macOS Homebrew installation, add the official tap with brew tap mongodb/brew and install with brew install mongodb-database-tools; the installation guide also instructs users to trust the tap with brew trust mongodb/brew. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/homebrew-brew · keywords: Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md
- [statement] On Linux, select the distribution and architecture in the Download Center. The installation guide offers a local .deb package installed with apt, an .rpm package installed with yum, or a .tgz archive. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md
- [statement] On Windows, install the separate Database Tools MSI or extract the Zip archive and copy the binaries from its bin directory. Add the directory containing the Tools to PATH to invoke them by name. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md
- [statement] Database Tools commands run in the operating-system command line. They are not commands to enter inside the MongoDB shell. (high confidence) — https://www.prisma.io/dataguide/mongodb/mongodb-database-tools · keywords: Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md
- [statement] The third-party Setup MongoDB Database Tools GitHub action documents an exact-version input, published SHA-256 verification, and a check that mongodump reports the requested version before caching the installation. These are the action author's documented behaviors. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/marketplace/actions/setup-mongodb-database-tools
- [statement] On macOS, the official Homebrew tap supports installing Database Tools alone: run brew tap mongodb/brew, then brew install mongodb-database-tools. The official repository describes this as a separate installation from Server and shell. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md · keywords: Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation · also: https://github.com/mongodb/homebrew-brew
- [statement] Separate Tools releases do not imply a separate manual install is always needed. The installation guide says a Server install through a system package manager may already include Tools; the official Homebrew repository explicitly says mongodb-community includes them. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md · keywords: Database Tools versioning, compatibility and installation · also: https://github.com/mongodb/homebrew-brew
- [statement] For Windows MSI and zip installations, the guide instructs users to add the installation or copied-binary directory to PATH so the tools can run by name. A successful installation alone does not establish that a command prompt can resolve the executable. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md
- [statement] The official Homebrew repository states that uninstalling mongodb-community does not uninstall the bundled Database Tools; removing Tools requires a separate brew uninstall mongodb-database-tools command. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/mongodb/homebrew-brew
